searchText: Hello, I wonder what is the most efficient way to compute the elligible/voted ether for a given epoch using beacon APIs ? I was looking at the beaconcha.in source code and it's using `/eth/v1alpha1/validators/participation`, but it's deprecated, right? <@!230439127164780546> For Prysm specific APIs you should ask in the Prysm discord. The standard APIs (supported by all other clients, and soon Prysm) are documented here: https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/ What you can do is query `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/validators` (with status filter), to get validators (and filter by slashed/not-slashed, active or not, etc.), then sum their effective balances. To get participant numbers I'm afraid the standard API doesn't offer what you want. The lighthouse API has some good API methods for this kind of thing though: https://lighthouse-book.sigmaprime.io/validator-inclusion.html Thanks a lot, I'm using Lighthouse, but I missed these APIs https://blog.lido.fi/the-road-to-trustless-ethereum-staking/ Largest ETH2.0 staking pools has some strong views on proof of stake. Honest question about ETH2 that I can’t really find an answer to. How will proof of stake alleviate the problems caused by attackers using under-priced opcodes to DoS the network with resource consumption attacks? <@456226577798135808> no, that’s something we need to fix at the execution level (and partially have in Berlin with EIP-2929) Does that mean chains that are just modified forks of ETH with PoS like BSC are still vulnerable to the same attacks? <vdWijden> Yes <vdWijden> Though BSC now uses geth woth snapshots enabled which mitigates some of the risk, but it also decreased blocktime and increased blocksize

excerpts.author: leruaa
excerpts.content: Hello, I wonder what is the most efficient way to compute the elligible/voted ether for a given epoch using beacon APIs ? I was looking at the beaconcha.in source code and it's using `/eth/v1alpha1/validators/participation`, but it's deprecated, right?

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
<@!230439127164780546> For Prysm specific APIs you should ask in the Prysm discord. The standard APIs (supported by all other clients, and soon Prysm) are documented here: https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/
What you can do is query `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/validators` (with status filter), to get validators (and filter by slashed/not-slashed, active or not, etc.), then sum their effective balances. To get participant numbers I'm afraid the standard API doesn't offer what you want. The lighthouse API has some good API methods for this kind of thing though: https://lighthouse-book.sigmaprime.io/validator-inclusion.html

excerpts.content: Thanks a lot, I'm using Lighthouse, but I missed these APIs
